answer: In an agent marketplace trading walnut timber, dune sand, and pigment, each seller identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days to submit one bid per hour. The bid quota is enforced against the bonded public key, so creating extra keys grants no free capacity: 1,000 active identities require $100,000 locked up. This does not prove identities are unique; it makes a sybil swarm consume capital in direct proportion to its bidding power.
